heading: TDS on Salary: Employer's Calculation Under the New Act
tldr: From April 1st, 2026, TDS on salary is governed by the new Income Tax Act 2025, replacing the 1961 Act.
Your employer deducts Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) from your salary based on your estimated annual income and declared investments.
The new Act retains the same income tax rates and slabs, but introduces changes to forms and section numbers for calculation.
Accurate investment declarations via Form 12BB are crucial to ensure your employer deducts the correct amount of TDS.
Form 16, issued by your employer, provides a summary of your gross salary, declared deductions, and the TDS deducted and deposited.
caption:
Your salary slip might look a little different from April 2026! A new Income Tax Act is changing how your employer calculates the tax they deduct from your pay. Don't worry, tax rates stay the same. But knowing about the new forms and how your investments are considered is key to paying the right amount of tax. Learn how it affects you in our latest article.
